COMMENTS: This individual was found to be heterozygous (monoallelic mutation carrier) for the MUTYH c.1187G>A (p.Gly396Asp) alteration. The MUTYH c.1187G>A alteration results in a missense change of Glycine to Aspartic Acid at residue 396 (p.Gly396Asp). This variant has been shown in multiple studies to co-segregate with disease in patients with autosomal recessive MUTYH-associated polyposis (PubMed 11818965 , 17489848). MUTYH p.Gly396Asp is one of the two most common pathogenic alterations present in a heterozygous state in approximately 1%-2% of individuals with northern European ancestry. Functional studies have shown that the p.Gly396Asp variant may impact MUTYH enzyme activity (PubMed 15987719 , 18534194). In summary, this well studied variant meets our criteria to be classified as Pathogenic. Monoallelic MUTYH mutation carriers: Although the data is mixed, a recent meta-analysis identified a minor increased risk for colorectal cancer with an odds ratio of 1.17 (95% confidence interval 1.01-1.34) associated with monoallelic MUYTH mutations (PubMed 23946381 ). However, family history is noted to further alter risk. Biallelic MUTYH mutation carriers: Biallelic MUTYH pathogenic mutations are causative of MUTYH-associated polyposis which is associated with an increased risk of colorectal polyposis and cancer. If a monoallelic MUTYH mutation carrier's partner is also a monoallelic carrier for a pathogenic MUTYH mutation, there is a 25% risk that each child would have two germline MUTYH pathogenic variants. Such individuals would have an increased risk for colorectal polyposis and cancer.

This heterozygous BRCA2 c.426-2A>G variant occurs in the invariant region (+/- 1,2) of the splice consensus sequence and is predicted to cause altered splicing leading to an abnormal or absent protein.This variant has been identified in 3/90370 of South Asian chromosomes by the Genome Aggregation Database (http://gnomad.broadinstitute.org) and has been reported in individuals with esophageal carcinoma and breast cancer (PMID: 32579544, 35710434, 31528241). Experimental RNA studies have demonstrated that this variant leads to exon 5 skipping (PMID: 32579544). In summary, this variant occurs in the invariant splice consensus sequence, has been reported in individuals with BRCA2 associated disease, and therefore is classified as pathogenic.  Pathogenic variants in BRCA2 cause BRCA2-associated Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer which is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by an increased risk for female and male breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and prostate cancers, as well as other cancer types (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1247/).  Relatives of an individual with a pathogenic BRCA2 variant have up-to 50% probability of carrying the same variant, and carriers are at an increased risk of developing BRCA2-associated disease.

This heterozygous BRCA2 c.5946delT variant is predicted to cause a frameshift, and leads to a premature termination codon 22 amino acids downstream (p.Ser1982Argfs*22). This alteration is predicted to lead to a truncated or absent protein, and truncating variants in BRCA2 are known to be pathogenic.  This variant has been identified in 0.6% of Ashkenazi Jewish chromosomes by gnomAD (http://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/).  This BRCA2 c.5946delT variant has been reported in many individuals and families with breast, ovarian, prostate, and pancreatic cancers and is considered a founder mutation in the Ashkenazi Jewish population (PMID: 9042909, 10417300, 22430266). In summary, based on the previous reports of this variant in individuals with BRCA2 associated disease and its truncating effect on the protein, this variant is classified as pathogenic. Note: BRCA2 c.5946delT is also known as BRCA2 6174delT.
